title: Filton6
summary: Four defendants from the Filton case were sentenced on 12 June 2026 after a judge found a terrorist connection; they have appealed. The original dossier also covers the initial six defendants and the wider Filton proceedings.
review_note: “Filton6” is the entry point for this research. The original dossier also covers the broader Filton 24/25 proceedings; counts, verdicts and sentences must be tied to the particular defendants and trial.

updates.title: Four sentenced with a terrorist connection; appeal filed
updates.summary: On 12 June 2026, Mr Justice Johnson sentenced four Filton defendants for criminal damage after finding a terrorist connection under section 69 of the Sentencing Act 2020. They filed an appeal in September.
paragraphs: A jury convicted Charlotte Head, Samuel Corner, Leona Kamio and Fatema Zainab Rajwani of criminal damage at the Filton factory on 6 August 2024; Samuel Corner was also convicted of inflicting grievous bodily harm on a police officer. None was charged with or convicted of a terrorist offence (sentencing remarks, paragraphs 1.1 and 3.1).

The judge found that the damage was serious, with well over £1 million paid by insurers, and that the offence was designed to influence the UK Government and to intimidate people working for Elbit and linked businesses. He rejected the argument that it was designed to influence the Israeli government (ruling, paragraphs 37, 39 and 46–49).

Head and Kamio received special custodial sentences of 6 years less 45 days, and Rajwani 5 years 8 months less 45 days, each including 1 year of extra licence. Corner received 8 years 8 months in total, including 3 years 8 months for grievous bodily harm. Each is subject to terrorist notification requirements for 15 years (sentencing remarks, paragraphs 6.3 and 8.1–8.4).

On 3 September 2026 their solicitors said an appeal had been filed against the sentences and the terrorist-connection finding. We have found no published decision on permission to appeal or hearing date.
This update covers these four defendants only. Other Filton trials are separate. For the law and a comparison with the Barclays5 ruling, read our legal study, Terrorist connection add-on.

corrections.text: The original annotation suggested that section 1 only refers to the UK government or an intergovernmental body. Section 1(4)(d) also includes the government of a country other than the United Kingdom. That annotation has been corrected; this does not determine whether the other statutory conditions were met in any particular case.

body_html:
Twenty-five people charged over an August 2024 action at Elbit Systems’ Filton site near Bristol, approximately £1.2m damage, split across multiple trials. Six acquitted of aggravated burglary in February 2026 with a hung jury on criminal damage; four convicted at retrial in May 2026; sentenced 12 June 2026 by Justice Jeremy Johnson with a “terrorist connection” finding — the first ever applied to protest criminal damage in the UK. Three further trials run into 2027.
